question: Can a sample-based neural saddle-point solver represent and recover both deterministic optimal-transport maps and stochastic optimal-transport plans for strong and weak costs at image scale?

key_findings.claim: The central contribution is an exact function-space maximin reformulation of weak optimal transport, followed by an approximate neural and finite-sample optimization procedure.
key_findings.evidence: An atomless auxiliary law and noise outsourcing represent each conditional plan as T(x,.)#S. Substituting this representation into the weak C-transform yields Cost(P,Q)=sup_f inf_T L(f,T), after an asserted interchange of infimum and integration. Algorithm 1 then parameterizes f and T by neural networks and alternates one potential update with k_T map updates; no Lipschitz constraint on f is imposed.

key_findings.claim: The paper proves representational density, not statistical consistency, optimization convergence, or recovery of an optimal plan by the trained networks.
key_findings.evidence: Theorem 1 says that on compact X and Z a neural network can approximate any fixed stochastic transport map in L2 and its output marginal in squared W2. It supplies no network-size rate, finite-sample bound, approximation of the transport cost or conditional law, or guarantee that SGAD reaches that network; the authors explicitly warn that the continuous approximator can be highly irregular and hard to learn.

key_findings.claim: Optimal-plan recovery is one-way for the evaluated costs, and the printed proof of the stronger strict-convexity lemma reverses two fundamental inequalities.
key_findings.evidence: Lemma 4 only shows that true OT maps occur among inner minimizers; the paper concedes that other, non-transport functions can occur. Lemma 5 would exclude them for costs strictly convex in the conditional measure, but neither the strong nor gamma-weak quadratic cost used experimentally is strictly convex. Its proof also prints C((mu+nu)/2) >= (C(mu)+C(nu))/2 for convex C and Cost >= L(f*,T1) although Cost=inf_T L requires the opposite signs. Flipping both signs repairs the intended contradiction argument, but the published derivation as written is invalid.

anchors.section: Appendix F, Equations 23-24 and proof chain

key_findings.claim: Strong quadratic transport collapses the conditional noise, while the weak variance term creates diversity through a task-defining trade-off rather than a generic anti-collapse guarantee.
key_findings.evidence: For gamma=0, a degenerate conditional distribution can minimize the strong C-transform, and the learned T empirically becomes independent of z. For gamma>0, subtracting conditional variance encourages mass splitting. The handbags-to-shoes sweep shows greater visual variety from gamma 0 to 1, but gamma=1 visibly loses input-style preservation; no quantitative diversity, fidelity, or coverage curve accompanies the sweep.

key_findings.claim: The toy weak-OT evidence validates conditional means for one specially tractable cost, not the full learned coupling in general.
key_findings.evidence: All toy experiments use gamma=1, where every optimum has a characterized conditional expectation. On two 2D pairs, the learned conditional mean obtains L2-UVP below 1% for Swiss roll and about 3% for eight Gaussians against a 2^10-sample discrete POT solution. The 1D study shows three neural restarts and four discrete optima visually, then infers near-optimal cost from agreement of conditional means. It reports no distance between full plans, marginal error, seed distribution, confidence interval, or test at 0<gamma<1.

key_findings.claim: On three unpaired-translation comparisons, NOT reports the best FID among the selected legacy baselines, but the study does not establish semantic correctness or a broad current image-translation advantage.
key_findings.evidence: Table 1 reports deterministic/stochastic NOT FIDs of 13.77/13.44 for handbags-to-shoes, 13.23/11.96 for male-to-female, and 25.50/25.97 for outdoor-to-church, lower than CycleGAN, DiscoGAN, AugCycleGAN, and MUNIT in their respective columns. The panel omits stronger setup-specific methods as out of scope, gives no human study or paired semantic metric, leaves the uncertainty protocol unexplained, and provides no uncertainty for one-to-one methods.

key_findings.claim: The visual evidence demonstrates smooth and diverse outputs, but also exposes that pixel-space optimality preserves incidental content and that the noise has no shared semantic coordinate system.
key_findings.evidence: Across Figures 5-7 and 12-22, color, background, pose, and texture frequently survive translation because pixel L2 rewards minimal change; anime hair can inherit background color, people remain visible in outdoor-to-church outputs, and semantically distant anime-to-shoes mappings have no correctness target. Latent interpolation is visually smooth, yet synchronized-noise Figures 23-24 show no consistent shoe or church attribute across inputs, which the authors explicitly acknowledge.

key_findings.claim: Training is materially expensive and explicitly unstable despite the compact two-network objective.
key_findings.evidence: Image runs use a ResNet potential, U-Net map, batch 64, k_T=10, and roughly 40,000 potential updates. Deterministic runs take one to three days on one 16GB V100; stochastic runs use four V100s because multiple noise samples are required. The authors report fluctuation and divergence in some saddle-point runs, especially when P is less dispersed than Q or gamma is high, and provide neither a convergence diagnostic nor compute-matched timing against baselines.

anchors.section: Appendix E, Optimization, stability, and complexity

key_findings.claim: The official release exposes the core implementation but does not provide a turn-key, internally matched reproduction of the paper.
key_findings.evidence: The MIT-licensed repository at current head 13850338a577b607a9a409c4c6cdfa26c60fc226 contains modular model/data helpers and six principal notebooks, but no tests, CI, package metadata, frozen environment, raw FID table, or experiment launcher. The two training notebooks have no saved outputs, require W&B and external target-stat files, and the requirements omit torch, torchvision, and wandb. The weak notebook defaults to Z_SIZE=8 although Appendix E says four; it evaluates test FID every 2,000 steps, while the plotting notebook loads a manually renamed T.pt without recording its run or step. Checkpoints are external rather than versioned with the code.

method.core_idea: Represent each conditional transport plan by a stochastic neural map T(x,z), insert this noise-outsourced representation into the weak Kantorovich semi-dual, and learn the map jointly with a target potential through stochastic maximin optimization.
method.mechanism: The potential rewards matching the target marginal, while the inner map minimizes a conditional transport cost minus potential value. An atomless z lets T express mass splitting. Strong costs need one Monte Carlo noise draw and tend to a deterministic argmin; weak quadratic costs estimate conditional variance from multiple draws, with gamma explicitly rewarding diversity. More map steps than potential steps approximate the inner minimization.
assumptions: Source and target are sample-accessible probability measures on Euclidean subsets and have the moments required by the chosen Wasserstein topology.
The weak cost is lower bounded, lower semicontinuous, convex in the conditional distribution, and has an estimable finite-batch form.
The auxiliary noise law is atomless and sufficiently expressive conditional maps can be optimized with the chosen neural architecture.
The infimum-integral interchange applies to the measurable function class used in the derivation.
A useful optimal dual potential exists and alternating stochastic ascent-descent finds a favorable inner minimizer.
The selected ground cost encodes the semantic correspondence desired by the downstream unpaired task.
Finite-sample marginal matching through a learned potential is an adequate proxy for the exact push-forward constraint.
For the stronger all-inner-solutions guarantee, the cost must be strictly convex in each conditional law, an assumption not met by the evaluated quadratic costs.

techniques.role: Outsources each conditional law through atomless noise so one neural map can represent stochastic plans.
Rewrites the weak C-transform as optimization over conditional stochastic maps.
Learns a target potential and transport map through the order sup_f inf_T.
Uses ten map updates per potential update to approximate the inner minimizer.
Builds unbiased Monte Carlo estimators for strong costs and corrected sample-variance weak costs.
Subtracts gamma times conditional variance to trade input similarity for stochastic diversity.
Uses squared pixel distance to encourage minimal visual change in unpaired translation.
Linearly raises gamma from zero during the first 25,000 potential iterations to ease stochastic training.
Concatenates a spatial Gaussian noise channel with the image and maps it through a U-Net.

evaluations.setting: Gaussian source to eight-Gaussian-mixture and Swiss-roll targets in 2D under the gamma=1 weak quadratic cost
evaluations.metric: L2 unexplained variance percentage of the learned conditional mean versus a 2^10-sample POT weak-OT solution, plus visual marginal and plan plots
evaluations.result: Below 1% L2-UVP for Swiss roll and approximately 3% for the eight-Gaussian mixture; generated marginals and mean maps look close to the discrete reference.
evaluations.baseline: One finite discrete weak-OT solution from POT, treated as ground truth

evaluations.setting: Two 1D Gaussian-to-mixture pairs under gamma=1, with three NOT restarts
evaluations.metric: Visual conditional-plan density, pushed marginal, monotone 1-Lipschitz conditional mean, and inferred near-optimal cost
evaluations.result: All three neural plans have conditional means visually similar to four nonunique discrete POT optima, but no numerical full-plan or marginal error is reported.
evaluations.baseline: Four random restarts of the discrete POT weak-OT solver

evaluations.setting: Deterministic and stochastic unpaired translation on handbags-to-shoes, CelebA male-to-female, and outdoor-to-church test splits
evaluations.metric: Test FID of translated source images against held-out target images
evaluations.result: NOT is best in all six selected one-to-one/one-to-many comparisons: 13.77/13.44, 13.23/11.96, and 25.50/25.97 respectively.
evaluations.baseline: DiscoGAN and CycleGAN for one-to-one; AugCycleGAN and MUNIT for one-to-many

evaluations.metric: Qualitative grids of multiple conditional outputs
evaluations.result: Visual diversity rises with gamma, while input-style preservation degrades at gamma=1; no LPIPS, conditional FID, precision/recall, or human rating quantifies the frontier.
evaluations.baseline: The same architecture and data at four gamma settings

evaluations.setting: Seven deterministic and six stochastic translation directions at 64 or 128 pixels
evaluations.metric: Selected output grids, latent interpolation grids, and synchronized-noise grids
evaluations.result: Outputs are generally plausible and interpolations smooth, but incidental input attributes persist and the same z produces no consistent semantic effect across inputs.
evaluations.baseline: Input images and, for three tasks, selected GAN translation outputs

limitations: The exact maximin equality does not imply that a finite neural SGAD solution is an OT map or even satisfies the target marginal.
Lemma 4 is only one-way; the evaluated strong and weak quadratic costs permit spurious inner minimizers because they are not strictly convex in the conditional measure.
The printed Lemma 5 proof reverses both the convexity inequality and the inequality implied by an infimum, even though its intended argument is repairable.
The infimum-integral interchange is invoked without checking the normal-integrand and measurable-selection conditions for the stated function space.
The universal-approximation theorem is nonconstructive and supplies no width, depth, sample, cost, conditional-law, or optimization rate.
All new weak-OT toy tests use gamma=1 and mostly assess the conditional mean, which cannot identify a nonunique full coupling.
No strong-cost toy experiment is run in this paper; performance is delegated to a prior deterministic-map benchmark.
Image evaluation covers three FID comparisons against 2017-2018 baselines and does not use paired semantics, human judgments, precision/recall, or modern translation alternatives.
The reported one-to-many error bars are not defined, while deterministic comparisons have no uncertainty and no seed protocol is stated.
Pixel L2 preservation is not equivalent to semantic identity and can retain backgrounds, people, color artifacts, or unrelated structure.
Gamma controls a cost-defined variance term, not disentangled or input-consistent semantic diversity; synchronized noise has no shared interpretable effect.
Training can fluctuate or diverge, has no convergence criterion beyond 'until converged,' and costs one to three V100-days or four V100s for stochastic maps.
There is no compute-, parameter-, or data-matched timing comparison with the baselines despite the simplicity claim.
Repeated test-FID evaluation during released training creates a model-selection leakage channel, and the paper does not separate a validation set.
The official notebooks do not pin the complete environment, retain the main run outputs, record the selected checkpoint lineage, or include automated tests and CI.
The released weak-training default uses eight noise samples per input rather than the four stated in Appendix E.
failure_modes: The learned map minimizes the objective for an approximate potential but pushes P x S to a distribution different from Q.
A fake inner solution attains the same semi-dual value while representing a non-optimal or non-feasible plan.
Strong-cost training ignores z and cannot represent required mass splitting.
High gamma prioritizes variance so strongly that the output loses correspondence with its input.
Low gamma yields conditional collapse and falsely appears deterministic even when the desired task is one-to-many.
The critic-map dynamics oscillate or diverge when the source is substantially less dispersed than the target.
Finite noise batches produce a noisy conditional-variance estimate and a biased practical optimization trajectory despite an unbiased point estimator.
A low marginal FID hides incorrect per-input correspondences, copied source content, or semantic label changes.
Pixel-space minimality maps a source to the visually closest target-like artifact rather than the intended semantic counterpart.
Latent interpolation is smooth but traverses entangled identity, color, geometry, and background factors.
A manually selected checkpoint exploits repeated test feedback or cannot be traced to the reported table.
A reproduction silently differs because code and paper use different noise-sample counts or incomplete dependency versions.
reusable_insights: Noise outsourcing is a clean modular interface between measure-valued conditional plans and ordinary neural functions.
Separate representational universality, population-objective correctness, empirical estimation, and optimizer convergence in every neural-OT claim.
Prove both directions of saddle-point recovery or explicitly test marginal feasibility to detect fake inner solutions.
Use a strictly convex conditional-law cost or an explicit feasibility mechanism when every optimizer must identify a valid plan.
Validate a stochastic plan with marginal discrepancy, conditional-law metrics, transport cost, and task utility rather than its conditional mean alone.
Treat diversity control as a Pareto frontier and report fidelity, coverage, semantics, and input consistency at each setting.
Ground costs are task specifications; pixel distance should be replaced or complemented when semantic preservation is the objective.
Give latent variables identifiable cross-input meaning if synchronized control is part of the claimed interface.
Use held-out validation for checkpoints and reserve the test split for a single final evaluation.
Publish exact configs, run IDs, per-seed raw metrics, checkpoint hashes, complete dependency locks, and executable tests.
open_questions: Which practical strictly convex weak costs preserve semantics while eliminating fake solutions at image scale?
Can marginal-feasibility certificates distinguish optimization failure from a theoretically spurious inner minimizer during training?
What finite-sample and finite-network error bound connects the neural maximin gap to plan cost and marginal violation?
Can a convergent single-level, extragradient, proximal, or smoothing method replace unstable alternating maximin updates?
How do four versus eight or more conditional noise samples affect variance-estimation bias, stability, compute, and diversity?
Does low FID persist against modern diffusion, flow-matching, Schrödinger-bridge, and dedicated translation baselines under matched compute?
How should full stochastic plans be benchmarked when optima are nonunique and only samples are available?
Can learned semantic or perceptual ground costs retain mathematical identifiability without importing label leakage or model bias?
Can the latent noise be factorized into stable cross-input controls while retaining optimality for a stated weak cost?
When does a stochastic transport plan provide better downstream calibration or decision utility than a deterministic Monge map?
Can training expose a reliable stopping signal based on duality gap, marginal discrepancy, and held-out transport cost?
How much of the image result is OT-specific versus architecture, target-FID checkpoint selection, and the inductive bias of U-Net skip connections?

competitive_landscape.title: Optimal Transport Mapping via Input Convex Neural Networks
competitive_landscape.difference: Makkuva et al. parameterize Brenier potentials with input-convex networks and recover deterministic quadratic-cost maps with structural guarantees. NOT removes convex architectures and adds stochastic weak plans, gaining flexibility while losing the same direct optimal-map identification.

competitive_landscape.title: Generative Modeling with Optimal Transport Maps
competitive_landscape.difference: Rout et al. use essentially the deterministic semi-dual/maximin mechanism for strong quadratic and embedded costs and evaluate restoration and generation. NOT's main algorithmic extension is atomless noise plus weak conditional costs, enabling mass splitting but introducing fake-plan ambiguity.

competitive_landscape.title: Score-based Generative Neural Networks for Large-Scale Optimal Transport
competitive_landscape.difference: Daniels et al. learn an entropy-regularized Sinkhorn coupling and sample its conditionals with Langevin dynamics, with convergence analysis for potential training. NOT targets unregularized strong and weak costs and amortizes conditional sampling in one map, but offers weaker recovery guarantees.

competitive_landscape.title: Do Neural Optimal Transport Solvers Work? A Continuous Wasserstein-2 Benchmark
competitive_landscape.difference: Korotin et al. build continuous pairs with known quadratic OT maps and show downstream generative quality can disagree with OT accuracy. NOT cites this benchmark for its deterministic special case but does not extend its exact-map evaluation to stochastic weak plans.

competitive_landscape.title: Kernel Neural Optimal Transport
competitive_landscape.difference: Kernel NOT explicitly proves that the present paper's weak quadratic objective may learn fake, non-distribution-preserving plans, then introduces strictly convex kernel weak costs to remove that ambiguity. It is the closest correction to the evaluated stochastic method.

competitive_landscape.title: Neural Optimal Transport with General Cost Functionals
competitive_landscape.difference: Asadulaev et al. extend neural stochastic-plan learning to costs over whole plans, add class- and pair-guided functionals, and provide recovery error analysis. This directly pursues NOT's proposed task-specific-cost direction and supplies stronger quantitative theory.

competitive_landscape.title: Entropic Neural Optimal Transport via Diffusion Processes
competitive_landscape.difference: ENOT models the dynamic Schrödinger-bridge form of entropic OT with a diffusion and fast learned inference, explicitly trading regularization bias for a unique smoother coupling. NOT is a static amortized map for unregularized weak costs and avoids iterative Langevin sampling.

competitive_landscape.title: Improving and Generalizing Flow-Based Generative Models with Minibatch Optimal Transport
competitive_landscape.difference: OT-CFM trains a continuous normalizing flow with a stable regression objective and minibatch couplings; with a true plan it approximates dynamic OT and supports translation. It largely avoids NOT's adversarial saddle training, though minibatch OT is only an approximation to the population coupling.

competitive_landscape.title: ENOT: Expectile Regularization for Fast and Accurate Training of Neural Optimal Transport
competitive_landscape.difference: Expectile-regularized NOT replaces near-exact nonconvex c-transform optimization with a regularized potential loss and reports up to threefold lower error and tenfold faster runtime on W2 benchmarks. It targets exactly the inner-optimization instability left open here, primarily for strong costs.

competitive_landscape.title: Neural Estimation Of Entropic Optimal Transport
competitive_landscape.difference: Wang and Goldfeld parameterize the entropic semi-dual and prove nonasymptotic neural approximation and sample-error bounds for both cost and plan, including minimax-rate results on compact supports. NOT's universality result lacks this statistical bridge from samples to a recovered coupling.

competitive_landscape.title: Overcoming Spurious Solutions in Semi-Dual Neural Optimal Transport: A Smoothing Approach for Learning the Optimal Transport Plan
competitive_landscape.difference: OTP derives conditions under which semi-dual maximin maps are genuine, then smooths the source and learns a plan to handle cases without deterministic maps. It directly addresses spurious solutions for standard quadratic OT and reports stronger one-to-many translation results than earlier semi-dual solvers.

novelty_assessment: NOT is a conceptually important bridge between weak optimal-transport theory and amortized neural conditional generation: noise outsourcing turns measure-valued conditionals into an ordinary map, and the resulting two-network maximin objective covers deterministic maps and stochastic plans in one template. Its 2022-era image results are strong against the selected baselines and its qualitative diversity control is compelling. The headline must nevertheless be narrowed. The exact contribution is a population function-space reformulation plus representational universality, not a guarantee that finite SGAD learns an OT plan. The strong all-solutions result excludes the quadratic costs actually tested and contains two reversed inequalities in print; Kernel NOT soon demonstrated concrete fake plans for the weak quadratic setting. Toy validation mostly checks conditional means at gamma=1, image validation relies on FID and visual grids, and the notebook release has configuration and checkpoint-lineage gaps. General-cost NOT, kernel costs, entropic neural OT, OT-CFM, expectile regularization, neural EOT error bounds, and OTP now offer more targeted costs, stabler optimization, statistical guarantees, or explicit spurious-solution remedies. The most valuable research direction is therefore certified stochastic-plan learning: pair expressive task costs with strict identification, measurable marginal/duality diagnostics, and full-plan benchmarks rather than extending the same unconstrained saddle objective unchanged.
reviewer_notes: Read all 34 cached pages, including every theorem and proof, the complete toy and image appendices, hyperparameters, compute disclosure, and comparison tables. Visually audited Figures 1-24: the grids substantiate plausible diversity and smooth interpolation but also show pixel-cost artifacts, retained non-target content, and no synchronized semantic meaning for z. Confirmed directly on page 24 that the published Lemma 5 proof prints both inequalities backwards; the intended proof can be repaired by reversing both. Audited official repository history and current head 13850338a577b607a9a409c4c6cdfa26c60fc226: initial public commit was 2023-02-07; implementation is notebook-centric with reusable source modules but no tests/CI or full environment lock; main training outputs are stripped; weak training defaults to eight noise draws versus four in the paper; test FID is logged throughout training; selected T.pt lineage is manual. The external checkpoint link reached a Yandex captcha in this environment, so checkpoint contents were not inspected. Checked eleven primary predecessor, benchmark, same-author corrective, general-cost, entropic, flow, statistical, stability, and spurious-solution papers through 2026-08-23.
